description: A homeowner wants to capture the exact failure pattern of an appliance before scheduling a technician, including when it fails, what sounds or signals appear, and whether the issue depends on load, time, or temperature.

user_profile.persona: 34-year-old resident who prefers to observe a problem carefully before paying for service
user_profile.context: The appliance does not fail consistently enough to describe clearly from memory alone
user_profile.communication_style: Detail-oriented and observant, values symptom logging more than immediate replacement

fact_sheet.fact: The appliance is a CryoCold Model 7 refrigerator/freezer combo unit.
The serial number of the CryoCold Model 7 is CC7-89B345K-01.
The appliance was purchased on June 15, 2021, from 'Appliance Universe'.
The manufacturer's 2-year warranty for the CryoCold Model 7 expired on June 15, 2023.
The homeowner's name is Alex Chen.
The appliance is located at the residence of 452 Maple Drive, Silver Creek, WA 98001.
The first failure was observed on October 10, 2023, at approximately 7:00 PM.
The primary symptom is that the refrigerator compartment stops cooling, while the freezer compartment remains fully functional.
During a failure on October 15, 2023, the internal refrigerator temperature reached 50°F (10°C).
The normal operating temperature set for the refrigerator is 37°F (2.8°C).
A low, continuous buzzing sound was heard from the back of the unit during the failure on October 10.
On October 15, a distinct clicking sound occurred every 5 minutes, lasting for approximately 2 seconds each time.
The digital control panel flashes the error code 'CF' when the cooling issue is active.
The failures typically last for a duration of 4 to 6 hours before normal cooling resumes on its own.
Failures have been occurring with a frequency of once every 2 to 3 days since the initial event.
The issue most commonly begins between 3:00 PM and 8:00 PM.
The ambient temperature in the kitchen is consistently maintained at 70°F (21°C).
The failure has occurred on days when the refrigerator is both lightly and heavily loaded with food items.
The refrigerator is located away from direct sunlight and has 3 inches of clearance on all sides for ventilation.
Alex Chen started a detailed failure log on October 11, 2023, using the 'SymptomLogger' mobile app.
On October 14, 2023, Alex cleaned the condenser coils, which were moderately dusty.
The cleaning of the condenser coils on October 14 did not prevent a subsequent failure on October 15.
A full power cycle (unplugging for 10 minutes) was performed on October 16 at 9:00 PM, which restored normal function for 12 hours.
Alex visually inspected the refrigerator door seals on October 17 and confirmed they are clean and create a firm seal.
Alex identified 'Apex Appliance Repair' as a potential service provider based on online reviews.
The contact phone number for Apex Appliance Repair is (555) 234-5678.
Apex Appliance Repair quoted a standard diagnostic visit fee of $125, which is applied to the total repair cost.

Alex's failure log shows a repeating pattern: the refrigerator compartment stops cooling while the freezer stays cold, the control panel flashes 'CF', buzzing or periodic clicking is heard, and the problem usually appears between 3:00 PM and 8:00 PM every 2 to 3 days.
After the condenser coils were cleaned on October 14, the same failure pattern returned on October 15, including the CF error, clicking sounds, and the refrigerator compartment warming to 50°F.

user_needs.description: What overall failure pattern have I observed with the refrigerator?
When was the failure first observed and how frequently does it occur?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After describing the main symptom, the user would naturally provide details on its timing and frequency.

user_needs.description: What specific sounds are associated with the failure?
What error code is displayed and what is the typical duration of a failure?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After describing audible symptoms, inquiring about visible symptoms like error codes and other temporal details like duration is a logical next step.

user_needs.description: What was the internal refrigerator temperature during a failure, compared to its normal setting?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After establishing the primary problem is a cooling failure, a detail-oriented user would likely want to quantify the failure by providing the exact temperature reached.

user_needs.description: After I cleaned the condenser coils, did the refrigerator still show the same failure pattern?
What was the effect of power cycling the unit?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After describing one troubleshooting action, it's common to list other actions taken.

user_needs.description: Which service provider has been identified and what is their diagnostic fee?
What are the model and serial number of the refrigerator?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After identifying the service provider and diagnostic fee, the next practical step is to gather the refrigerator's model and serial number for the service call.

user_needs.description: On what date did the manufacturer's warranty expire?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Once the specific appliance has been identified by its model number, checking its warranty status is a very common and practical next step before incurring service costs.

user_needs.description: Have the failures been dependent on the food load in the refrigerator?
